observed_fact: Coinbase reported that criminals bribed and recruited rogue overseas support agents who abused customer-support access and stole data
source_assessment: Coinbase stated that the data was used to facilitate social-engineering attacks and that the company received a USD 20 million extortion demand
my_assessment: Legitimate support access can be converted into criminal intelligence that increases the success of customer fraud without directly exposing private keys or passwords
confidence: High for company-reported facts; moderate for the full criminal structure
alternative_explanation: Different insiders may have had different knowledge or intent and public reporting may not describe all access paths
decision_relevance: SOC, fraud, insider-risk, HR, procurement, legal and customer-support teams need a shared investigation model
source: Coinbase — Protecting Our Customers: Standing Up to Extortionists

observed_fact: FBI IC3 reported global BEC exposure exceeding USD 55 billion and continued use of banks, payment processors and cryptocurrency services
source_assessment: FBI describes BEC as compromise or impersonation of trusted business identities used to cause unauthorised transfers
my_assessment: The decisive control point is often the payment or supplier-change workflow rather than the email filter alone
confidence: High for the scale and fraud model
alternative_explanation: Complaint data may underreport or inconsistently classify incidents and not every loss involves mailbox compromise
decision_relevance: Email, identity, supplier-master and payment data must be correlated and recall action must begin quickly
source: FBI IC3 — Business Email Compromise: The USD 55 Billion Scam

observed_fact: FS-ISAC and Akamai reported finance as the top target for volumetric DDoS attacks and described a multi-bank attack with multi-day outages
source_assessment: The report assessed that DDoS had evolved from nuisance activity into a strategic operational threat
my_assessment: Financial institutions should detect material service degradation and customer impact rather than alerting only on traffic volume
confidence: High for sector reporting; moderate when generalising to every organisation
alternative_explanation: High traffic may reflect legitimate demand and some attacks may produce little disruption
decision_relevance: DDoS monitoring must connect network telemetry to customer transactions, service levels, provider dependencies and DORA resilience processes
source: FS-ISAC and Akamai — From Nuisance to Strategic Threat

observed_fact: The European Supervisory Authorities designated critical ICT third-party providers in November 2025
source_assessment: The designation process considered systemic importance, support for critical financial functions and service substitutability
my_assessment: Supplier concentration is now an active supervisory concern as well as a technical threat-model issue
alternative_explanation: Designation does not mean that a provider is insecure or that all clients face identical risk
decision_relevance: Financial entities need dependency registers, contractual evidence, exit strategies and incident coordination for critical providers
source: European Banking Authority — DORA critical ICT third-party provider designation

observed_fact: Current standards and tools support structured CTI, automated exchange, behaviour mapping and portable detection formats
source_assessment: OASIS, MITRE, MISP and Sigma provide complementary models for representing intelligence and translating it into defensive operations
my_assessment: The value of CTI is measured by validated searches, detections and decisions rather than the volume of received indicators
alternative_explanation: Tools may be deployed poorly and automation may amplify low-quality intelligence
decision_relevance: Every shared indicator requires context, confidence, lifecycle and testing before automated enforcement
source: OASIS STIX/TAXII; MITRE ATT&CK; MISP; SigmaHQ

observed_fact: The FBI reported that Kali365 lures users into entering attacker-supplied device codes on the legitimate Microsoft page and captures access and refresh tokens
source_assessment: The FBI assessed that the platform lowers the barrier for less-technical attackers through AI lures, templates, target tracking and token capture
my_assessment: A legitimate login page can become part of a phishing chain when the user authorises the attacker's device; password reset alone may not end the incident
confidence: High for the FBI-reported mechanics; moderate for sector-specific victim prevalence
alternative_explanation: Some device code events are legitimate and the public alert does not describe every victim
decision_relevance: Financial SOCs need device-code, token, mailbox and SaaS activity rather than relying only on URL reputation and password reset
source: FBI IC3 — Kali365 Phishing-as-a-Service Kit Hijacks Microsoft 365 Access Tokens

event_or_activity: UNC1069 fake meeting and ClickFix intrusion
observed_fact: Mandiant reported a compromised Telegram account, fake Zoom meeting, ClickFix instruction and reported AI-generated video in an intrusion against a cryptocurrency-sector fintech entity
source_assessment: Mandiant attributed the activity to UNC1069 and described seven malware families in the compromised environment
my_assessment: The attacker combined real-account trust, video interaction and user-executed commands to overcome individual suspicion signals
confidence: High for the source-reported intrusion; moderate for one unified operator structure
alternative_explanation: Different operators may share tooling and the exact role of the AI-generated video may vary
decision_relevance: Fintech organisations must monitor messaging, developer endpoints and meeting-based social engineering in addition to email attachments
source: Mandiant — UNC1069 Targets Cryptocurrency Sector with New Tooling and AI-Enabled Social Engineering

observed_fact: GTIG reported that an axios maintainer account was compromised and malicious releases introduced plain-crypto-js to deploy WAVESHAPER.V2 on multiple operating systems
source_assessment: GTIG attributed the campaign to UNC1069 based on malware evolution and infrastructure overlaps
my_assessment: A single maintainer-account compromise can place developer credentials, CI/CD systems and downstream financial applications at risk at scale
confidence: High for the published campaign; moderate when estimating every downstream impact
alternative_explanation: Not every installation contained valuable secrets and some affected systems may have been isolated
decision_relevance: Financial firms need dependency inventories, build provenance, maintainer security and developer EDR as part of transaction-system security
source: GTIG — North Korea-Nexus Threat Actor Compromises Widely Used Axios NPM Package

event_or_activity: Selective delivery of financial phishing and malware
observed_fact: The FBI reported that TDS infrastructure can profile visitors and show safe content to non-targets while redirecting selected victims to financial phishing or malware
source_assessment: The FBI assessed that TDS use supports scams, ransomware access and evasion of security research
my_assessment: A single sandbox result may not reproduce the victim experience; redirect chain and victim context are evidence
confidence: High for the FBI warning; moderate for prevalence of specific targeting rules
alternative_explanation: Content variation may also result from legitimate geolocation or marketing systems
decision_relevance: SOC, fraud and brand-protection teams need full URL-chain collection and post-click account monitoring
source: FBI IC3 — Cyber Criminals Redirecting Users to Fraudulent Websites with Malicious Traffic Distribution Systems

event_or_activity: Negative time-to-exploit and AI-assisted vulnerability research
observed_fact: Mandiant reported a mean time-to-exploit of negative seven days and GTIG reported an AI-assisted zero-day exploit assessment
source_assessment: The publishers assessed that exploit development and attacker workflows are accelerating
my_assessment: Financial institutions must assume that public-facing applications may be compromised before a CVE, patch or IOC exists
confidence: High for the stated reporting; moderate when generalising the pace to every product
alternative_explanation: The observed mean reflects Mandiant's case set and not all vulnerabilities are actively targeted
decision_relevance: Inventory, segmentation, compensating controls, application logging and retrospective hunting are as important as patch speed
source: Mandiant and GTIG — 2026 AI and vulnerability research
